children: BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - The China stock market has finished lower in four straight sessions, retreating almost 100 points or 2.7 percent in that span. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just above the 3,580-point plateau and it may open to the downside again on Wednesday.

The global forecast for the Asian markets is negative on rising oil prices and hostilities in the Middle East. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourses are expected to follow that lead.
The SCI finished modestly lower on Tuesday as losses from the property and technology companies were mitigated by support from the financial sector.

For the day, the index fell 17.99 points or 0.50 percent to finish at 3,584.58 after trading between 3,565.59 and 3,604.98. The Shenzhen Composite Index dropped 18.42 points or 0.90 percent to end at 2,033.97.
The lead from Wall Street remains bleak as the major averages opened lower on Tuesday and remained well under water throughout the day, ending near session lows.

The Dow plunged 848.75 points or 1.64 percent to finish at 50,759.42, while the NASDAQ dropped 181.37 points or 0.74 percent to close at 24,328.38 and the S&P 500 sank 76.06 points or 1.03 percent to end at 7,340.53.

The weakness on Wall Street came amid lingering concerns about the outlook for Nvidia (NVDA) ahead of the release of the AI leader's fiscal third quarter results after the close of trading. After the bell, Nvidia beat expectations on the top and bottom lines and offered strong guidance for the fourth quarter.
Reports of an outage for a highly classified network that the National Security Agency uses for its internal communications also added to jitters about the country's technology infrastructure.
Technology stocks weighed, while finance, oil, housing and utility stocks also showed moves to the downside and gold stocks bucked the downtrend.

Crude oil regained some ground on Tuesday amid concerns about increasing tensions in the Middle East after tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery rose $0.35 or 0.4 percent at $86.07 a barrel.
